newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma fails to bring back Soviet symbols.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma fails to bring back Soviet symbols.

text.p: Russian parliamentarians gave strong backing to a bid to bring back the hammer and sickle emblem of the former Soviet Union on Wednesday, but failed to gather enough votes to force through the constitutional changes they sought.

A total of 239 of the 450 deputies in the State Duma lower house of parliament voted to bring back the red flag emblazoned with the hammer and sickle, while 255 said the stirring old Soviet anthem should replace the tamer Russian one.

But bringing back Soviet-era emblems is tantamount to constitutional change in the new democratic Russia and the support of two thirds of deputies -- 300 votes -- would have been needed for the changes to go ahead.
The tsarist symbol of a double-headed eagle has been Russia's official emblem since 1993 and the white, blue and red tricolour flag has replaced the red and gold Soviet one.
No words have yet been written to Russia's new anthem, which comes from Ivan Glinka's opera Life for the Tsar.
